digest.component_or_area: LLM sub-call routing and model class configuration
propositions: Four hand-built sub-call sites pass config=cfg without declaring a model class, causing them to inherit cfg.model instead of honoring the configured model class vocabulary, regardless of how three model classes are configured on Bedrock.

The overlap-judge sub-call dominates plan-review traffic with 18 of 23 LLM calls, all routing to direct Anthropic instead of configured Bedrock, making a class-only cutover ineffective for the majority of plan-review traffic.

The ticket-digest sub-call runs on the store write path (enrich_drain.maybe_drain invoked during rebar comment and create operations), sending ticket content to Anthropic during routine operations with no gate context or verdict disclosure.

A regression test must configure model classes differently from cfg.model to distinguish between calls honoring class configuration versus calls inheriting the raw cfg.model value, as both configurations resolve to the same provider when cfg.model equals the class default.

Three of four sub-call sites (ticket-digest, overlap-judge, code-novelty) must select their model class explicitly from the vocabulary with documented reasoning, while spec_scan._scan_epics_inner is a top-level op's primary call and deliberately kept on cfg.model.

An AST-based provenance guard must prevent future hand-built sub-calls from silently inheriting cfg.model while a class table is configured, by tracing config= expressions and flagging raw LLMConfig.from_env at the end of the chain.
